# Bast v0.9.0 release checklist

This checklist covers the first Bast release with native Windows support. Complete it in order. The stable release workflow runs only from a pushed `v*` tag.

## Progress

Verified on 2026-08-19:

- [x] Artifact Signing account, identity validation, and Public Trust profile
- [x] Entra application, service principal, and exact GitHub OIDC federation
- [x] Profile-scoped `Artifact Signing Certificate Profile Signer` role
- [x] Protected GitHub `artifact-signing` environment, secrets, and variables
- [x] Release and nightly Windows jobs bound to the signing environment
- [x] Installer pinned to the expected certificate subject
- [x] Signed workflow rehearsal
- [x] Rehearsal artifacts and temporary signing branch rule removed
- [ ] Pull request and merge
- [ ] Nightly Windows 11 acceptance testing
- [ ] Stable v0.9.0 release
- [ ] WinGet submission

## Current signing resources

- Artifact Signing account: `ellipse`
- Resource group: `ellipse`
- Region: West Europe
- Endpoint: `https://weu.codesigning.azure.net/`
- Certificate profile: `ellipse`
- Profile type: Public Trust
- Expected publisher subject: `CN=ellipse Software Group Limited, O=ellipse Software Group Limited, STREET=45 Fitzroy St, L=London, C=GB, PostalCode=W1T 6EB`

The identity validation and certificate profile were active on 2026-08-18. Recheck their status before release.

## 1. Configure keyless GitHub authentication

Use a Microsoft Entra application and GitHub OIDC. Do not create a client secret.

Create an application and its service principal:

```sh
client_id="$(az ad app create \
  --display-name bast-github-actions \
  --query appId \
  --output tsv)"

az ad sp create --id "$client_id" --output none

sp_object_id="$(az ad sp show \
  --id "$client_id" \
  --query id \
  --output tsv)"

subscription_id="$(az account show --query id --output tsv)"
tenant_id="$(az account show --query tenantId --output tsv)"

printf 'Client ID: %s\nTenant ID: %s\nSubscription ID: %s\n' \
  "$client_id" "$tenant_id" "$subscription_id"
```

Create one federated credential. The subject below uses the repository's current immutable GitHub OIDC prefix. Recheck the prefix before creating the credential if the repository has been renamed or transferred.

```sh
gh api repos/ellipse-software/bast/actions/oidc/customization/sub

az ad app federated-credential create \
  --id "$client_id" \
  --parameters '{
    "name": "bast-artifact-signing",
    "issuer": "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com",
    "subject": "repo:ellipse-software@186202678/bast@1310381514:environment:artifact-signing",
    "description": "Bast release and nightly signing jobs",
    "audiences": ["api://AzureADTokenExchange"]
  }'
```

The issuer, audience, and subject must match exactly. Do not use the conventional `repo:ellipse-software/bast:...` subject for this repository while its API reports the immutable prefix above.

## 2. Grant the signer role

Limit the service principal to the `ellipse` certificate profile:

```sh
profile_scope="/subscriptions/$subscription_id/resourceGroups/ellipse/providers/Microsoft.CodeSigning/codeSigningAccounts/ellipse/certificateProfiles/ellipse"

az role assignment create \
  --assignee-object-id "$sp_object_id" \
  --assignee-principal-type ServicePrincipal \
  --role "Artifact Signing Certificate Profile Signer" \
  --scope "$profile_scope"
```

Verify the assignment:

```sh
az role assignment list \
  --assignee-object-id "$sp_object_id" \
  --scope "$profile_scope" \
  --query '[].{role:roleDefinitionName, scope:scope}' \
  --output table
```

Do not grant Contributor, Owner, or subscription-wide signer access to the GitHub identity.

## 3. Create the GitHub signing environment

Create an environment named exactly `artifact-signing`:

```sh
printf '{}' | gh api \
  --method PUT \
  repos/ellipse-software/bast/environments/artifact-signing \
  --input -
```

Store the Azure identifiers as environment secrets:

```sh
gh secret set AZURE_CLIENT_ID \
  --repo ellipse-software/bast \
  --env artifact-signing \
  --body "$client_id"

gh secret set AZURE_TENANT_ID \
  --repo ellipse-software/bast \
  --env artifact-signing \
  --body "$tenant_id"

gh secret set AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID \
  --repo ellipse-software/bast \
  --env artifact-signing \
  --body "$subscription_id"
```

Store the signing resource names as environment variables:

```sh
gh variable set AZURE_ARTIFACT_SIGNING_ENDPOINT \
  --repo ellipse-software/bast \
  --env artifact-signing \
  --body 'https://weu.codesigning.azure.net/'

gh variable set AZURE_ARTIFACT_SIGNING_ACCOUNT \
  --repo ellipse-software/bast \
  --env artifact-signing \
  --body 'ellipse'

gh variable set AZURE_ARTIFACT_SIGNING_PROFILE \
  --repo ellipse-software/bast \
  --env artifact-signing \
  --body 'ellipse'
```

Restrict the environment to deployments from `master` and tags matching `v*`. If a second maintainer can approve deployments, add a required reviewer. Do not enable prevent-self-review when there is no independent reviewer available, because it will make releases impossible.

## 4. Bind signing jobs to the environment

Add this job-level field to `build-windows` in both `.github/workflows/release.yml` and `.github/workflows/nightly.yml`:

```yaml
environment: artifact-signing
```

The jobs already request only these permissions:

```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write
```

Keep `azure/login` configured for OIDC. Do not add an Azure client secret.

## 5. Pin the installer publisher

Replace the broad publisher match in `apps/web/public/install.ps1` with an exact comparison against:

```text
CN=ellipse Software Group Limited, O=ellipse Software Group Limited, STREET=45 Fitzroy St, L=London, C=GB, PostalCode=W1T 6EB
```

Confirm the exact value from a signed test artifact before merging:

```powershell
$signature = Get-AuthenticodeSignature .\bast.exe
$signature.Status
$signature.SignerCertificate.Subject
```

Pin the stable publisher subject, not the certificate thumbprint. Artifact Signing rotates short-lived signing certificates.

`install-nightly.ps1` delegates to `install.ps1` with the nightly channel selected, so the same publisher check covers both channels.

## 6. Prepare and merge the Windows changes

Create a focused branch from the current worktree:

```sh
git switch -c feat/windows-support
git add .
git commit -S -m "feat: add native Windows support"
git push -u origin feat/windows-support
gh pr create
```

Require these checks before merge:

- Go tests on Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows
- Go race tests and vet
- Web lint and production build
- CodeQL

Protect `master` and release tags before publishing. Require pull requests and passing checks for `master`. Restrict creation of tags matching `v*` to maintainers.

## 7. Signing rehearsal completed

The branch rehearsal completed successfully before merge. Both Windows archives were signed and the release workflow is now tag-only. Inspect the downloaded executables on Windows:

```powershell
Get-AuthenticodeSignature .\bast.exe | Format-List Status, StatusMessage, SignerCertificate
.\bast.exe --version
```

The status must be `Valid`, and the certificate subject must exactly match the expected publisher. The temporary `feat/windows-support` deployment branch and rehearsal artifacts have been removed. The `artifact-signing` environment now accepts only `master` and protected `v*` tags.

## 8. Rehearse the full Windows release path

Run the nightly workflow from `master`:

```sh
gh workflow run nightly.yml --ref master
```

Test on Windows 11 x64:

```powershell
irm https://bast.sh/install-nightly.ps1 | iex
bast --version
bast update
```

Also test Windows 11 ARM64 on real ARM64 hardware before claiming ARM64 runtime support. Cover:

- installation and user `PATH` updates
- OpenSSH detection and SSH config parsing
- local and remote shells
- PowerShell PSReadLine history import
- key creation, import, and Windows ACLs
- file browser, SFTP, upload, and download
- in-process self-update and rollback behavior

## 9. Handle the first stable Windows installer bootstrap

Until v0.9.0 exists, GitHub's latest stable release points to v0.8.1, which has no Windows ZIP. Publishing the Windows install command before v0.9.0 therefore causes a missing-asset failure.

Use one of these release sequences:

1. Merge runtime, CI, release workflows, and the unadvertised installer. Publish v0.9.0, then merge and deploy the public Windows documentation.
2. Make the stable PowerShell installer detect a release without Windows assets and report that Windows builds begin with v0.9.0. Keep the public install command hidden until the release is available.

Do not leave a public install command that fails with a generic GitHub 404.

## 10. Prepare the immutable release

Write and review the release notes before pushing the tag. Create a draft release first so the workflow can add assets and publish it:

```sh
release_sha="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"

gh release create v0.9.0 \
  --draft \
  --target "$release_sha" \
  --title "Bast v0.9.0" \
  --notes-file /path/to/v0.9.0-notes.md
```

Review the draft title, notes, and target commit before continuing.

## 11. Publish v0.9.0

Release only from a clean, verified `master`:

```sh
git switch master
git pull --ff-only
git status --short
git tag -s v0.9.0 -m "Bast v0.9.0"
git push origin v0.9.0
```

The tag push triggers publishing and the Homebrew update.

The published release must contain 16 assets:

- four Unix `.tar.gz` archives
- four Unix `.tar.gz.sha256` files
- two Windows `.zip` archives
- two Windows `.zip.sha256` files
- `SHA256SUMS`
- `EllipseSoftware.Bast.yaml`
- `EllipseSoftware.Bast.installer.yaml`
- `EllipseSoftware.Bast.locale.en-US.yaml`

Verify that the draft was resumed rather than replaced, all checksums match, both Windows executables have valid signatures, and the Homebrew formula update completed.

## 12. Verify stable installation and updates

On clean Windows 11 x64 and ARM64 machines:

```powershell
irm https://bast.sh/install.ps1 | iex
bast --version
bast update
```

Confirm that:

- `bast --version` reports `v0.9.0`
- the executable is installed under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Bast` by default
- a new PowerShell session can resolve `bast`
- Authenticode status is `Valid`
- updating an existing install succeeds
- a failed update restores the prior executable

## 13. Submit WinGet after release

Validate the three generated `EllipseSoftware.Bast*.yaml` manifests against the immutable v0.9.0 assets, then submit them with WinGetCreate. Test both fresh install and upgrade after the manifests are accepted:

```powershell
winget install EllipseSoftware.Bast
winget upgrade EllipseSoftware.Bast
```

Advertise WinGet only after the manifest has merged into `microsoft/winget-pkgs` and the public command resolves successfully.
